ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that $P$ is the centroid of $\triangle ABC$. Connect $AP$ and extend it to intersect $BC$ at point $D$. If the area of $\triangle ABC$ is 20, what is the area of $\triangle ADC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $P$ is the centroid of $\triangle ABC$,

it follows that $AD$ is the median of $\triangle ABC$,

hence, the area of $\triangle ADC$ is equal to half the area of $\triangle ABC$,

and since the area of $\triangle ABC$ is 20,

thus, the area of $\triangle ADC$ is $\boxed{10}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First, describing the diagram: The image shows triangle ABC with A at the top, B on the lower left, and C on the lower right. Segment AP is drawn from A through an interior point P and continues to meet side BC at D (D is the intersection point on BC, although it is not visibly labeled in the picture). Now reasoning: Since P is given as the centroid of triangle ABC, the line from vertex A through P meets BC at the midpoint D, so AD is the median from A. Therefore BD = DC. Triangles ABD and ADC have equal bases BD and DC on the same line BC and share the same altitude from A to BC, so their areas are equal. Together they form triangle ABC, whose area is 20. Hence area(ADC) = 1/2 × 20 = 10.
